claims.statement: An Airtable OAuth integration owner can generate an optional client secret that authenticates the integration when requesting an OAuth token; Airtable does not store a copy and it is not recoverable.

sources.supports: A client secret is an optional private key that authenticates your integration when requesting an OAuth token.
the client secret is **not recoverable**, as Airtable does not store a copy of your client secret.
`Authorization` (optional) | **Required** if your integration has a `client_secret`. **forbidden** if it does not.

claims.statement: When an integration has a client secret, Airtable requires an Authorization header on token creation and token refresh requests with the value Basic {credentials}, where credentials is the base64 url-encoding of {client_id}:{client_secret}; the header is forbidden for an integration without a secret. The page documents the secret in this header only, not as a body field.

sources.supports: `Authorization` (optional) | **Required** if your integration has a `client_secret`. **forbidden** if it does not. The value should be the interpolated string "`Basic {credentials}`", where `credentials` is the base64 url-encoding of the interpolated string "`{client_id}:{client_secret}`".
